text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Romania harvested 85 percent of its 1997 wheat crop.
- Romanian motorists will have to pay a fuel tax according to the capacity of the tanks of their cars when leaving the country, the paper said.
- A barge carrying 2,000 tonnes of iron ore ran aground in the Black Sea port of Constanta.
- Scores of Romanian private companies failed to cash in export earnings from, the paper said.
- Staff made redundant in mines earmarked for closure will get the equivalent of up to 20 monthly wages.
- The Roman SA truck factory in Brasov will cut 1,000 jobs this week, the paper said.
- The Romtelecom RA telephone operator plans to raise tariffs starting September 1.
- The government decided to use 25,000 tonnes of wheat from state reserves.
- Restructuring and layoffs at the Copsa Mica chemical plant might trigger labour unrest, the paper said.
